doc.title: Marshall Allen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 19, 2021

title: The music library and adapting parts
summary: Allen has an overwhelming archive of music, cannot recall all the parts after decades, and adapts and changes them.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: What is the state of the music library? You still have a great deal of that printed, actual hand written music?
Yeah. I had all of it, all the music was left here and I had so much music it’s overwhelming.
Yes I can imagine. And the music, the parts he had written for some certain size group which of course now have changed, and if you pull out —

Well if I can remember, I mean in the early days when he left I could remember all — I tried to put this puzzle together you see, because it was fresh on my mind but now it’s been what, twenty, thirty years? You know the parts kind of get away so I’ll go in another direction for what I feel.
You mean you’ll adapt the piece for your own interpretation and what you have now?

Yeah. Well I’ve got to do it, because I can’t remember all the jigsaw puzzles and all the different parts of Sun Ra because he was always changing stuff. So that left it open to me, whatever — I’m used to it being changed, so I change it.
